A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CEI convergence study. The main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figure 1 report original CEI simulations on two synthetic problems and five benchmark problems, including repeated-run results.

after.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Figures 1–2 report original CEI simulations on eight synthetic configurations and the five retained benchmark problems.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and standard CEI remain unchanged. However, new Remark 3.16 introduces a tolerance variant: feasibility becomes c(x) ≤ λ, and the acquisition's feasibility factor becomes Φ((λ−μc)/σc). This is a limited procedural extension, although it is not separately evaluated.

E1.justification: The synthetic coverage expands from two 2D cases, RKHS-SE and GP-Matérn, to combinations of RKHS/GP, SE/Matérn and dimensions 2/4. This adds synthetic function-family combinations and 4D scenarios within the same optimization task. All five benchmark problems remain; Banana is renamed Rosenbrock.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate CEI without competing optimization algorithms. References to other CBO methods and theoretical comparisons with Bull do not constitute evaluated empirical baselines.

E3.justification: The reported synthetic generation changes: GP sampling uses 1000 uniformly chosen points instead of a 30×30 grid, while RKHS functions are described as kernel sums with standard-normal coefficients instead of posterior means of Gaussian samples. The expanded synthetic study specifies 50 optimization iterations. The retained benchmark definitions, simple-regret metric and maximum-likelihood fitting procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The expanded synthetic study checks whether convergence persists across both kernels and dimensions 2 and 4. Section 4.2 also newly reports similar benchmark performance with Matérn and SE surrogates, adding limited kernel-sensitivity evidence. Neither version provides component ablations or noisy-observation robustness experiments.

E5.justification: The retained benchmarks still report 100 independent trials with median and 25th/75th-percentile curves. However, v1's two synthetic plots also display percentiles, whereas v2's replacement synthetic plots show single curves without uncertainty displays or an identified aggregation statistic.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 1 replaces the two earlier synthetic trajectories with eight reported convergence curves, substantially expanding the synthetic result set. These use revised settings and therefore do not establish same-setting performance gains. The five benchmark plots in v1 Figure 1(c–g) are reproduced unchanged in v2 Figure 2; their convergence findings remain the same.

T1.justification: The Bayesian analysis changes from GP assumptions on both objective and constraint to a GP objective with RKHS constraints, a convex domain and a revised Lipschitz assumption. New Lemma C.3 and rewritten Appendix C arguments introduce time-dependent confidence bounds and different index selection, adding a sqrt(log t) factor to the Bayesian rates. v2 also adds sample-complexity Corollary B.5 and tolerance-related derivations, restricts the Matérn information-gain lemmas to ν > 0.5, and removes v1's positive-part Lipschitz lemma.

C1.justification: v1 claims identical frequentist and Bayesian rates with both functions GP-sampled; v2 narrows the Bayesian claim to the objective and claims similar rates with an additional logarithmic factor. The introduction also restricts improvement over Bull to specified dimension/smoothness regimes and adds ν > 1/2 to the Matérn claim. The claim of first convergence rates for CEI is retained.

C2.justification: New Remarks 3.14–3.16 substantially expand applicability and mechanism discussion: noisy constraints make feasibility and the incumbent ambiguous, noisy-objective regret may be negative, and tolerance changes feasibility and the constraint-dependent bound. Remark 3.8 also qualifies when the information-gain rates improve on earlier bounds, replacing v1's blanket interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, M1 hardware with 16 GB memory, 10d initial samples for synthetic experiments, and explicit SE-kernel use for the retained benchmarks. These improve documented reproducibility; the PDFs do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Targeted additions include Lin et al., another Iwazaki work, and optimization references supporting tolerance; Calandra, Lederer and Jiao references disappear. The comparison with Bull is narrowed. v2 also removes the explicit attribution of the retained EI-deviation lemma to Wang et al. (v1 Lemma C.4, v2 Lemma C.5), although that work remains cited elsewhere.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and much of the prose remain intact. Local restructuring separates synthetic and benchmark experiments, renames the Bayesian section, relocates the initial-feasibility discussion, and revises the abstract and contributions. Author/header text and citation presentation also change.

P2.justification: The central experimental display changes from one seven-panel figure to eight synthetic log-log panels plus a separate five-panel benchmark figure. Two synthetic contour figures disappear; the three retained benchmark contour figures are consolidated, with captions changing 'feasible' to 'infeasible.' Document typography, margins, title/author layout and running headers also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by qualifying the comparison with Bull and explicitly revising the Bayesian assumptions, proof construction and logarithmic rates. Added code-access and experimental details improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by losing synthetic percentile displays and by GP-sampled constraint experiments that do not directly match the revised RKHS-constraint assumption, supporting a limited overall improvement.
